post.description:
Creates a bulk upload in a group of the organization and returns a signed URL and headers for the file upload.

To complete a bulk upload:
1. Call this endpoint with the `group_guid` for the new links. Set `domain` to a custom domain of the group. Set `upload_type` to the item that each row creates: `link` for a link, `qr_code` for a QR code, or `coupled_link` for a link and its QR code. For `qr_code` and `coupled_link`, also set `template_id`.
2. Send the file in a `PUT` request to `upload_url`. Include every header in `headers` without changes, including `Content-Type`. The upload fails if any header is different. The file can be up to 25,000,000 bytes (25 MB), and a larger file gets `400 EntityTooLarge`. The URL is valid until `upload_url_expires_at`.

Processing is asynchronous. When it is complete, Bitly emails a report to the user's verified primary email address and to the organization admins. The report shows the result and the short link for each row. The request returns `400 INVALID_EMAIL` if the user has no verified primary email address.

File format: the first row must contain the column headers. Each other row describes one item to create. `Long URL` is the only required column. The optional columns are `Title`, `Tags` (comma-separated if more than one), `Backhalf`, `Expiration` (for example `2030-01-31T15:04:05+0000`), `UTM Source`, `UTM Medium`, `UTM Campaign`, `UTM Term`, `UTM Content`, and `Current Bitly Short Link`. A row with `Current Bitly Short Link` changes the destination of that existing link and does not create a new link. A `qr_code` upload ignores the `Backhalf`, `Tags`, and `Current Bitly Short Link` columns. The maximum number of rows in one file depends on the plan. For examples, see [How do I shorten links in bulk?](https://support.bitly.com/hc/en-us/articles/360056277331) and [How do I create QR Codes in bulk?](https://support.bitly.com/hc/en-us/articles/25227111392397-How-do-I-create-QR-Codes-in-bulk).

get.description: Returns the status of one bulk upload. The status is `pending` after the file is uploaded and before processing starts, then `in_progress`, and then `success`, `partial_success`, or `failure`. When processing is complete, `report_url` links to the report. Every member of the organization can see the bulk uploads of all its groups. A bulk upload whose file was not uploaded returns 404.

parameters.description: The `id` returned when the bulk upload was created.
parameters.name: bulk_upload_id
